title: Observe the Passover night as a vigil for the Lord

context_note: The verse calls this night a vigil for the Lord for all Israel throughout its generations. The vigil is the continuing observance of the night of departure.
verse_text: [12:42] It is a night vigil for the Lord, to bring them out of the land of Egypt. This same night is a vigil for the Lord for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.

title: Apply the stated circumcision and participation rules for the Passover meal
original_audience: Israelite hosts and the people seeking to eat Passover
context_note: Verse 48 expressly prohibits any uncircumcised person from eating and permits a resident foreigner to participate when the stated circumcision condition is met. Verses 43–45 set out the earlier household and eligibility distinctions.
verse_text: [12:43] The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the law of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it. [12:44] And every man’s household slave, or one bought with silver, you shall circumcise; and then he shall eat of it. [12:45] A sojourner or a hired worker shall not eat of it. [12:48] But if a resident foreigner comes to you to keep the Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male belonging to him; and then he shall draw near to keep it, and shall be as the native of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
